_comment: Verified display-number to bank-id map for SHOSMED_LF3_Chemistry_Batch7_Review.txt.
HOW THE MAP WAS VERIFIED. The review supplied ORIGINAL IDENTIFICATION SIGNATURES,
so the map was derived by FULL CONTENT MATCH and not inferred from display numbers,
a presumed contiguous run, topic alone or the answer pattern:
1. Each signature was parsed from the review: original stem plus all four original
option texts. The per-item expected keys were reassembled independently and
reproduced the review key block and its A=7/B=27/C=18/D=8 tally exactly.
2. Each signature was matched against all 485 chemistry records on a canonical form
that decodes HTML entities, strips tags, folds <sub>/<sup> and Unicode sub- and
superscripts to plain digits, normalises dashes, quotes, Greek letters and arrows,
lowercases and collapses whitespace. ALL 60 MATCHED EXACTLY ONE RECORD.
3. No two records anywhere in the 485-record chemistry bank share a full signature,
and no two share even a canonical stem, so no match was ambiguous.
4. Every stored answer letter agreed with the review letter for that display number,
and every stored topic agreed with the signature topic.
CONTIGUITY IS A RESULT, NOT AN ASSUMPTION. The 60 verified ids happen to run
chem-362 .. chem-421 consecutively, in display order, but that was derived from the
content match rather than assumed and then checked.
NO OVERLAP with chemistry batches 1-6 (359 earlier ids), so all 60 displays are
newly reviewed unique ids and coverage moves 359 -> 419 of 485.
TWO THINGS THE REVIEW ASKED TO CHECK RATHER THAN ASSUME, both resolved before editing:
- Q22's exponent is ALREADY a real exponent in the stored field: the record holds
"remaining = initial x (1/2)<sup>n</sup>". The "(1/2)n" appearance in the review
source was a plain-text extraction artifact, not a stored or rendered defect, so
nothing was changed there.
- The standalone 'Unanswered' and 'Report an issue' labels appear in NO stored field
anywhere in the bank (629 biology + 485 chemistry records were searched). They are
UI text, so they were not touched and are not reported as a data correction.

notes: The review instructs that for EDITED items the keyed and distractor headings be
synchronized with the actual option texts, and that KEEP items and the points-only
item are exempt. Many stored distractor headings were abbreviated rather than the
full option text, so synchronization expanded them; that is an instructed change.
The review also writes prime marks as U+2032 in its replacement prose. The bank uses
the ASCII apostrophe throughout and stores no U+2032, and the review's own rule 4 says
to match existing punctuation conventions without a bank-wide cleanup, so replacement
prose uses the ASCII apostrophe. This is a presentation choice, not a content change.
